Marathon Petroleum's stock gained a fraction today, holding near $363.54 after bouncing back yesterday from a sharp dip. The modest move reflects a stabilization in energy markets following days of geopolitical turbulence—U.S. oil prices sit at $83.90 a barrel while refineries are running at a very high 97.4% capacity, which supports refiner margins. With gasoline and diesel inventories at comfortable levels (206.8 and 103.4 million barrels respectively), there's no supply crunch pressuring margins downward at the moment.

The broader picture is one of elevated but uncertain energy demand: Middle East tensions (Iranian negotiations, tanker attacks, and Strait of Hormuz concerns) have kept oil prices elevated, and Europe's low gas storage ahead of winter could sustain global energy prices higher. A refiner like Marathon benefits from this sustained price environment when capacity utilization stays this high, though geopolitical de-escalation efforts—like Qatar's talks with Iran today—could just as easily ease tensions and moderate crude prices downward.
